You can cast spells, drawing on the magic your patron has granted you. See chapter 7 of the Player's Handbook for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Blood Hunter spells, which appear on the Warlock spell list.

Cantrips. You know two cantrips of your choice from the Warlock spell list. You learn an additional Warlock cantrip of your choice at 10th level.

Spell Slots. The Profane Soul Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of levels 1–4, as well as the level of those slots; all your slots are the same level. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a Short or Long Rest. To cast one of your level 1+ spells, you expend a spell slot.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells available for you to cast, choosing from the Warlock spell list. To start, choose two level 1 Warlock spells. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Blood Hunter levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the table. Each spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one spell on your list with another Warlock spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Warlock spells.

Spell Save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Spell Attack Modifier = your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Spellcasting Focus. You can use a weapon for which you have an active Crimson Rite as a Spellcasting Focus for your Warlock spells.
